questions.question: New private repo name for the rewritten dstrader history?

options.label: dstrader-rewritten (Recommended)
options.description: Matches the option description you picked. Clear semantic. Lives alongside `dstrader` (current, untouched) and the future `dstrader-public`. You'd later decide whether to retire current `dstrader` or use the rewritten one as the new daily-driver.

options.label: dstrader-r2
options.description: Round-2 suffix style — mirrors how FamilyFund tracks rewrite generations. Shorter; readable as "second sanitization pass".

options.label: Replace current dstrader (rename current to -archive)
options.description: GitHub-rename existing `dstrader` to `dstrader-archive` (frozen reference) and push the rewritten history to a fresh `dstrader`. This makes `dstrader` continuously the daily-driver name. Higher coordination cost — redirects any local clones / remotes / CI references. Owner-only action; agents don't rename repos.

questions.question: Worker strategy for stripping the DSTrader.jar blob?

options.label: Strip by exact blob SHA (Recommended)
options.description: `git filter-repo --strip-blobs-with-ids` against the single SHA `6a916308086c8c2e9e90f859ff98f1b983f3cc17`. Most targeted; touches the fewest commits; deterministic; verifies the SHA is no longer reachable post-rewrite.

options.label: Strip all *.jar from history
options.description: `git filter-repo --path-glob '*.jar' --invert-paths`. Catches any other jar that ever existed in history (belt-and-braces). Slightly broader blast radius if there's a jar we care about (there shouldn't be — `*.jar` is now gitignored).

options.label: Strip all blobs > 1 MB
options.description: `git filter-repo --strip-blobs-bigger-than 1M`. The option in your earlier pick. Same effect as SHA-strip today (worker confirmed only this one >1MB blob exists), but future-proofs against other large binaries.

## Worker reply triaged — FINDINGS, one decision point

**Mechanically clean:** strict gitleaks HEAD=0/ALL=0, all Step-2 greps explainable (46 IB hits all synthetic `U0000003-5`/`DU0000001-2`; 3 envlike all shell-var FPs), 0 workflow secrets (security-scan.yml only, default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, no fork-exfil), files-suspicious empty.

**The single finding:** `DSTrader.jar` (~MB Java build artefact) reachable from `main` history. Removed at HEAD by `850e5c2` (#4), `*.jar` is now gitignored, so no recurrence. But under the adopted **6a mirror push**, all history goes to `dstrader-public` — the blob would be retrievable via `git cat-file` from the public repo, not in the public HEAD tree.

**Why this is non-trivial despite "gitleaks-clean":** strict gitleaks treats the blob as binary and doesn't text-scan it. A jar built from pre-sanitization source can carry, inside compiled class files / SourceFile attributes / embedded resources, content that the Step-2 tree grep cannot see — e.g. pre-#2 `/Users/dtogni/...` paths embedded in debug info, or pre-#3 string literals if the build pre-dated those scrubs. Strict gitleaks's clean verdict doesn't dismiss this risk; it just confirms no signature-rule hit.

**This is exactly the scope of existing ticket dstrader#1 / #19** — "HUMAN-ONLY follow-up to #7: filter-repo cleanup of audit residuals." The jar blob is an audit residual.
